ORDINANCE 2 OF 2021

AN ORDINANCE TO PERMIT BRANDON HILLENBURG AND HILLENBURG
HEAT & AIR TO DO BUSINESS WITH THE CITY OF CABOT; DECLARING
AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, Ark. Code Ann § 14-42-107(b)(1) states that no alderman, council
member, official, or municipal employee shall be interested, directly or indirectly, in the
profit of any contract for furnishing supplies, equipment, or services to the municipality
unless the governing body of the city has enacted an ordinance specifically permitting
alderman, council members, officials, or municipal employees to conduct business with
the city; and

WHEREAS, the City was in need of reliable HVACR services in early 2020 and
solicited sealed bids in order to retain a service provider. Hillenburg Heat & Air returned
the lowest sealed bid and on March 27, 2020, entered into an agreement with the City of
Cabot to provide HVACR system preventative maintenance and service; and

WHEREAS, Brandon Hillenburg was sworn in as a City Council Member on
January 1, 2021. He was not a member of the Cabot City Council when Hillenburg Heat
& Air entered into an agreement with the City in March of 2020. Furthermore, neither he
nor Hillenburg Heat & Air has done any business for the City since he was sworn in as a
City Council Member, pending passage of this ordinance.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: Brandon Hillenburg and Hillenburg Heat & Air are hereby
permitted to conduct business with the City of Cabot, Arkansas to the extent authorized in
their agreement with the City, attached hereto as Exhibit “A”. This agreement was
previously entered into after all state and local laws were complied with, including all
competitive bidding procedures.

SECTION 2: This Ordinance only gives authority for the services delineated on
Exhibit "A", attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference, and for none other.
The authority given herein applies only to that activity which is specifically permitted and
is the extent of the approval of that authority for the time period referenced herein.

SECTION 3: This Ordinance shall be in effect until December 31, 2022.

SECTION 4: There is HVACR work which currently needs to be completed in

CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS
Special Council Meeting Minutes
January 1, 2021

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on social
distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot moved the monthly
Council Meeting to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508 N. Lincoln, as advertised.
This allowed for spacing between chairs, as suggested. The event was successfully
streamed through YouTube. You may view this’ meeting at
https://fb.watch/2QzeqzXxheN/.

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the Special Meeting of the Cabot City
Council at 9:08 a.m. on January 1, 2021 in the Veterans Park Event Center.
Mayor Kincade opened with prayer and led the Pledge of Allegiance. This
meeting followed a Swearing In Ceremony for all Council Members.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present: Ed
Long, Michael Jones, Stephen Redd, Brandon Hillenburg, Maggie Cope, James
Reid, Matt Webber, and Ron Waymack. Others present: City Attorney Ben
Hooper, City Paralegal Jessica Hooper and City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy
Yocom.

Motion 4 read legislation by title only oy Mr. Reid, fecond by Mr. Webber.
Motion passed unanimously by a Roll Call Vote.

DECLARING AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES was read by City Clerk

AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING THE ORGANIZATION AND PROCEDURE OF THE
CITY COUNCIL; ESTABLISHING COMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS; REPEALING
CONFLICTING LEGISLATION; DECLARING AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER
PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the City Council of Cabot, in keeping with its statutory duty, has convened to
organize its meetings and procedures for the coming year; and

WHEREAS, the City Council desires to maintain a committee structure in order to better and
more efficiently serve the residents of Cabot; and

WHEREAS, legislation conflicting with the current will of the City Council as expressed in this
ordinance should be repealed.

NOW THEREFORE BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: This governing body hereby adopts procedures to organize itself as delineated
in Exhibit “A” attached hereto and incorporated herein by this reference. City council committees
and committee assignments for 2021 shall be as delineated in Exhibit “B”, also attached hereto and
incorporated by reference.

SECTION 22: If any provision of this Ordinance or its attachments, or the application thereof
is held invalid, such invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of the Ordinance, and to
this end, the provisions of this Ordinance are declared to be severable.

SECTION 3: All prior ordinances, resolutions, code sections, any other legislation, and any
parts thereof in conflict with this legislation are hereby repealed; this specifically includes Ordinance
6 of 2020.

SECTION 4: It is essential for the health and safety of the City of Cabot for the City Council
to be organized in order to address serious and pressing concerns that may arise within the community.
An emergency is therefore declared and this ordinance being necessary for the preservation of the

public peace, health, safety and welfare shall be in full force and effect from and after its passage.

City Council Meeting Organizational Structure
1. Work Session Meetings

Work Session meetings (also referred to as Agenda Meetings) shall be held on the first
Monday of every month at 6:30 p.m. These Work Session meetings are utilized to allow council
members and each standing committee to discuss details of proposed legislation with City staff in
a more informal setting. The Work Session shall be called to order by the Mayor who will then
recognize the chair of each committee in turn to discuss the items on the agenda relevant to that
committee. Each committee chair shall preside over the discussion of agenda items relevant to his
or her committee and may conduct votes amongst his committee members to forward any piece of
proposed legislation on to a regular council meeting or for any other appropriate purpose. No
readings or votes for final passage of legislation shall be conducted during Work Session meetings.

At the conclusion of each Work Session meeting, a Regular Session Council meeting shall
be held. At this meeting any formal reading, votes for final passage, or other appropriate action
may be taken in regards to any motion or piece of legislation. This meeting need not be conducted
if there are no items on its agenda for consideration.

2. Regular Session Meeting

The City Council shall meet in Regular Session meeting on the third Monday of each month
at 6:30 p.m. At these meetings any formal reading, votes for final passage, or other appropriate
action may be taken in regards to any motion or piece of legislation. Pursuant to state law, these
meetings shall be presided over by the Mayor, with each council member having an opportunity
to discuss any item, make any appropriate motion, and vote when appropriate.

Only items on the agenda may be discussed, read, or voted on, unless the agenda is
amended to add that particular item by 2/3 vote of all elected council members. An item not on
the agenda may be discussed, though not voted on, during the community input section of the
meeting.

Pursuant to state law, any motion to suspend the rules, waive readings, approve or attach
an emergency clause, or similar motion must be passed by 2/3 vote of all elected council members

3. Location

The Cabot City Annex is the regular meeting place for the Cabot City Council. The
Veterans Park Event Center or other appropriate location may also be used if needed.

4. Dates of Meetings

If any of the prescribed dates or times for Work Session or Regular Session meetings fall
on a holiday or other inopportune time, the Council may select a new date and time for that

articul ting.

5. Agendas for Meetings

The agenda for the Work Session meetings shall be coordinated by the Mayor's office.
Any council member may request to have an item added to a Work Session meeting agenda. A
Work Session agenda, along with appropriate documents, should be forwarded to council
members by 4:00 p.m. on the Thursday before the meeting if possible.

The agenda for the Regular Session meetings shall be coordinated by the Mayor's office.
Items may be placed on this agenda by the Mayor or by majority vote of the appropriate
committee at a Work Session meeting or other committee meeting. A Regular Session agenda,
along with appropriate documents, should be forwarded to council members by 4:00 p.m. on the
Thursday before the meeting if possible.

In order to be placed on an agenda, a legislative item must be sponsored by either a
council member or the Mayor. Ifa legislative item is forwarded to the Council from one of the
city’s independent commissions it must be sponsored by that independent commission.

Agendas are considered final once forwarded to council members and legislative items
may not be added after that point except upon 2/3 vote of all elected Council members. However,
an item may be added to the agenda after it was sent out but before the start of the meeting upon
joint agreement of the Mayor and the City Council President Pro Tempore.

6. Committees and President Pro Tempore

City Council committees and committee assignments shall be as delineated in the
attached Exhibit B. Ed Long, as longest serving member of the Cabot City Council, is hereby
named City Council President Pro Tempore.

7. Mayor and City Council Relationship

In exercising its management responsibilities, the City Council reserves its authority
to approve policy which represents broad statements of its intentions, approves plans and
programs, and delegates authority of administration to the Mayor, except those rights that
are by law conferred upon or reserved to the city council. The City Council delegates the
authority to the Mayor to hire capable personnel within an approved wage and salary policy,
to plan and establish schedules and to train, supervise and terminate employees. Per A.C.A.
§ 14-42-110, the City Council reserves the authority to review the hiring or removal of a
department head and may overturn the hiring or removal of a department head by the Mayor
upon two-thirds majority of all elected Council members.

8. Further Responsibilities of the Mayor

The Mayor has the principal responsibility for directing the operations of the city
government and for advising and assisting the City Council in its deliberations. In connection
with the latter responsibility, the City Council requests the Mayor to furnish it with whatever
data, information, and material it may need to properly carry out its functions in an informed

--- page 7 (OCR) ---
manner.

The Mayor also has the principal responsibility to ensure that the city's administrative
officers and department heads understand and obey all local, state, and federal laws
pertaining to the city's operations, and when a violation of any law is discovered, that
immediate disclosure is made to the City Council and proper and adequate disciplinary
measures are taken against the responsible employee or employees.

9. Further Responsibilities of the Council

It is the responsibility of City Council members to be engaged and present at meetings in
representing the residents of Cabot. If any member of the City Council is absent for either three
consecutive meetings or four total meetings in a calendar year then a Resolution of Reprimand
shall be considered by the Council. Absences may be excused at a council member’s request and
by joint agreement of the Mayor and the President Pro Tempore of the City Council.

It is the further responsibility of council members to hold themselves to a high ethical and
moral standard in representing the residents of Cabot. Any member who fails to live up to these
standards or who brings embarrassment or disrepute to the City Council may also be subject to a
Resolution of Reprimand.

10. City Council and Mayor Cooperation

Efficient management of the city can exist only through mutual understanding and
complete cooperation between the City Council and the Mayor. The Mayor's performance
cannot be of the best unless he is given the latitude to exercise independent judgment in
executing policies of the City Council. The City Council acknowledges that obligation and
gives the Mayor the latitude of judgment and discretion, and expects faithful performance in
carrying out the policies of the City Council.

It shall be understood that administrative authority for the management of the city
rests with the Mayor. Members of the City Council should refrain, as individuals, from giving
specific direction or instruction to city personnel pertaining to the discharge of assigned
duties, however, open communication between aldermen and city employees is encouraged
and expected to guarantee sound decisions based upon the free flow of information.

December 15, 2020 at 6:30pm
Veterans Park Community Center
508 North Lincoln, Cabot, Arkansas 72023

I.

Call to Order/Roll Call
Maggie Cope called the meeting to order at 6:30 pm.
Present: Maggie Cope, John C. Thompson, Greg Sled, Nick Whitaker, Tricia Ambeau, John Rudd,
Sheila DeArmond
Guest: Attorney Greg Crumpton
Former Parks and Recreation Commission member Eric Park presented Maggie Cope with a
plaque for her 9 years of service to the commission. Tonight will be Ms. Cope’s last meeting as
a commissioner.

II.

Minutes of Regular Meeting
Minutes from the meeting held on November 17, 2020 were presented. NICK WHITAKER
MOTIONED TO ACCEPT THE MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 17, 2020, SECOND BY JOHN C.
THOMPSON. ALL SAY AYE.

III.

Financials
General Director, Travis Young, presented the November 2020 financials. SHELIA DEARMOND
MOTIONED TO ACCEPT THE NOVEMBER 2020 FINACIALS AS PRESENTED, SECOND BY GREG
SLED. The monthly financial were standard. Uniforms for basketball and wrestling have been
ordered. A&P deposit put us back where we should be financially. ALL SAY AYE IN PASSING
THE NOVEMBER 2020 FINANCIALS.
Programs
Program Director, Lorenzo Mendoza, presented the program report. Basketball has begun
practices with the season play beginning January 4th. One court at each gym will be used at the
Community Center, Cabot Freshman Academy, and Cabot Junior High North. Registration was
down compared to last years numbers with 395 players and a total of 56 teams. Fifty kids are
registered in the wrestling program and a lot of the tournaments have already been canceled.
Basketball will be able to allow 25 spectators for each team. All teams have coaches.
Several youth sports associations have submitted their end of season reports.
Cabot Youth Football – nothing to report at this meeting.
Panther Flag Football stated the season was successful with little issues.
Cabot Youth Cheer – nothing to report at this meeting.
BMX – nothing to report at this meeting.

IV.

77

V.

VI.

VII.

Construction/Directors Report
General Director, Travis Young, provides an update. All outdoor park areas are being
winterized. The only major project we have at this time is installing French Drains on softball
field #1 with all but 2 completed. Maintenance workers are taking some of their time off after
working hard all summer. Comp time has been managed well.
Christmas lunch for employees will be held tomorrow with Red River Auto Group, Crown
Trophy, and Cabot Emergency Hospital sponsoring the event. Social distancing will be
practiced.
Old Business
Worker Comp. – The bid from the City of Cabot went to BITCO. The park department will
continue to follow the city with the same company. John Rudd asked why we did not shop with
local business. The park will stay with the City on this bid until we have our own HR
department and then discuss other options. JOHN C. THOMPSON MOTIONED TO FOLLOW THE
CITY WITH THE SELECTION OF BITCO TO COVER THE PARKS DEPARTMENT WORKMANS COMP.
POLICY, SECOND BY TRICIA AMBEAU, ALL SAY AYE, MOTION PASSES.
New Business
American Legion Contract - The Richie Road fields will be contracted to the legion for use by
their baseball program. The contract was discussed. Raising the insurance to reflect
$1,000,000.00 instead of $100,000.00 and wording was discussed. Standard insurance with
American Legion will be sufficient. NICK WHITAKER MOTIONED TO APPROVE THE CONTRACT
WITH AMERICAN LEGION WITH THE CHANGE MADE TO REFLECT $1,000,000.00 DOLLAR
REQUIREMENT, SECOND BY JOHN RUDD, ALL SAY AYE, MOTION PASSES.
Budget 2021 – The budget cannot be finalized until A&P has completed their budget. A&P did
not have a meeting this month. The most up to date are reflected in the packet that were
received today. A&P gives us 75% of actuals each year. A&P should have a 6% increase in 2021.
The only changes in the budget are within employee benefits for the upcoming year. The HR
and IT position are in the budget but will be tabled until March. Without assistance from the
City of Cabot, the proposed positions of HR and IT may not be possible. Most of our revenue
comes from gate and concessions. Nick Whitaker would like to have a full budget meeting once
A&P has finalized their numbers. The budget discussion for 2021 will be tabled until January.

78

Bond Project Committee – Would the commission be interested in forming a committee to
work on future Bond Projects? A short list of names from the commission member and citizens
from the community will be created for those who would like to serve on the committee.
Memorials (Bench/Tree) – Discussion was about creating guidelines for memorial benches or
trees for individuals who have passed away. Organization have asked about placing memorials
in parks or at facilities. Staff would like to place a bench at the pond in memorial to Jim
Bledsoe, front desk staff, that passed away due to Covid19.
Board Elections – Nomination for Chairman - Nick Whitaker nominated Greg Sled for
Chairman, second by John C. Thompson, all say aye. Nominations for Co-Chairman –. John
Rudd nominated Shelia DeArmond, second by Greg Sled, all say aye.
VIII.

Community Input
The park department did receive the Arkansas Parks and Recreation Grant for 2021. Shades for
the softball fields will be ordered followed by pickleball and the outdoor fitness park. The
mountain bike will be addressed this year. The proposed pedestrian trail from Metro plan was
discussed.

and as such are unsafe and hazardous and a breeding place for rats, rodents and other

menace to abutting properties, with the current condition of said structures not being fit
for human habitation; and because of such conditions, the City Council declares the same
to be condemned as a public nuisance and is ordered abated, removed or razed by the

CITY OF CABOT, ARKANSAS
Council Meeting Minutes
January 25, 2021

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on
social distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot
moved the monthly Council Meeting to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508
N. Lincoln, as advertised. This allowed for spacing between chairs, as
suggested. The event was successfully streamed through YouTube. You
may view this meeting at
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zohHr84MUOA .

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular meeting of the Cabot City
Council at 6:30 p.m. on January 25, 2021 in the Veterans Park Event
Center. Council Member Matt Webber led the prayer and Council Member
Brandon Hillenburg led the Pledge of Allegiance.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present:
James Reid, Matt Webber, Brandon Hillenburg, Ed Long, Maggie Cope, and
Michael Jones. Stephen Redd attended the meeting via Zoom. Council

“EXHIBIT A”

Engineering Consultant
Scope of Services

Unless otherwise specifically stated within this Agreement, the following shall be considered the “Scope
of Services” for the purpose of defining the Consultant’s scope of services:

A.

Plan Review Services: The Consultant shall provide technical review of, and answer inquiries
relating to: site plans, subdivision plans, improvement plans, land disturbance plans,
construction plans and escrows relating to projects proposed by applicants to be developed
within the City and within the City’s Planning Jurisdiction to ensure that such conform to codes
adopted by the City.

City Project Design: The Consultant shall provide Engineering and other applicable services to
design a full array of public works type projects including transportation infrastructure systems,
storm water management systems, street repair design, minor and major drainage system
designs, etc.

Environmental Services and Regulatory Agency Interactions: The Consultant shall interact
with, and comply with all regulations of State, Federal and Local entities including, but not
limited to: Arkansas Department of Transportation, Arkansas Department of Agriculture,
Arkansas Natural Resources Commission, Arkansas Department of Environmental Quality, U.S.
Army Corps of Engineers, Federal Emergency Management Agency, Federal Highway
Administration, United States Environmental Protection Agency.

Grant Assistance: The Consultant shall, as requested, complete or assist in the completion of
grant applications for City projects.

Surveying, Easements and Related Services: The Consultant shall provide boundary surveys,
topographic surveys, construction staking, prepare easement plats and easement documents, and
assist in easement acquisition.

CAD and GIS Services: The Consultant shall provide, as requested, computer-aided drafting
and geographical information system capabilities.

Meeting Attendance and Participation: The Consultant shall be expected to attend a variety of
City meetings, including but not limited to: Planning Commission meetings, City Council
meetings, meetings with affected property owners, meetings with City staff and developers, and
meetings with State, Federal or other local entities.

Work Product: The Consultant shall provide to the City copies of all work products without
limitation, which shall include reports, analyses, correspondences, plans, proposals, submittals,
schematics, exhibits, drawings and any other documents produced in connection with the
consulting relationship with the City in printed form, as well as in electronic form to include
portable document form and the root file(s).

Assignment of Professional Engineer: The Consultant shall assign to the City a minimum of one
(1) staff person who is a Professional Engineer licensed to practice in the State of Arkansas.
Responsiveness: The Consultant shall commit to provide services to the City in a timely manner,
on or before and applicable deadline dates, without reasonable delays.

Dear Mr. Martin:

Please accept this letter as notice that the City of Cabot (hereinafter referred to as the City)
intends to purchase real property and all buildings/structures located on that real property from
Keith Martin, Revocable Trust (hereinafter referred to as Seller). The purpose of this letter is to
summarize our discussions thus far and to note our intentions regarding the proposed transaction,
subject to the approval of the Cabot City Council. Based on our discussions, it is my intent that
the purchase would be under the following broad terms with other details to be worked out through
the contract negotiation process:

1. The property and buildings/structures to be sold are located at 2102 S. 2"4 Street, Cabot,
Arkansas 72023.

2. The purchase price is $235,000 and the property will be sold “as is”.
3. Seller does not intend to include appliances, equipment or furniture in the transaction.

4. The intent to purchase will be publicly discussed on Monday, February 1, 2021 and
will be disclosed to the council and the public January 28, 2021.

Please note, this is only a Letter of Intent and should not be construed as a binding
agreement or an offer to enter into a binding agreement. The City does not have the authority to
enter into a binding agreement in this matter without the formal approval of the Cabot City
Council. If you are in agreement with these terms, please sign below and return the original to my
office. The City will then proceed in seeking authorization to enter into a binding agreement
consistent with this letter.

AFFIDAVIT

A request is hereby made to the City Council for permission to destroy (recycle via compactor
and/or shredder) outdated records and materials of the Cabot Police Department. Due to lack of
storage space, it has become necessary to destroy these documents and allow current data
adequate space to be stored.

Per statute Arkansas Code Annotated § 14-2-204, case files and support documents are to be
maintained for a period of at least seven (7) years; therefore, the Chief of Police requests that
the following support documents dated prior to January 1, 2014 be destroyed:

Arrest Records
Incident Reports
Accident Reports
Jail Logs

Radio Logs

The Chief of Police will not destroy any documents required by the State of Arkansas to be
permanently maintained and will comply with Arkansas Code Annotated §§ 12-12-104 and 14-2-
203(b)(1) and that the records related to crimes of violence as defined by Arkansas Code
Annotated § 5-42-203 will be kept permanently. All documents previously mentioned for
destruction are included in the auditing process. Since the City of Cabot is audited annually, the
documentation has already been part of prior audits.

A little about myself, I’m a Native Arkansan born and raised in Crossett and a
1988 graduate of Fort Smith Southside High School. I joined the US Army
Reserves at the age of 17 and went on active duty shortly after graduating high
school. During this time, I attended Central Texas College and Maryland State
University along with many other military training and technical schools. I am a
Persian Gulf War Veteran and served a tour of duty with the Multinational Force
and Observers on the Sinai Peninsula along with a tour of duty in Germany before,
during, and after it’s unification. After leaving the military in 1993 I became
employed by ABF Freight Systems in North Little Rock. Shortly thereafter, in
1994, I moved to Cabot and currently continue a 27 year career with ABF Freight.
I am married to Melissa Little and have 3 children. My two sons are Cabot High
School graduates and our daughter currently attends Cabot Central Elementary. My
family and I attend Austin Station Baptist Church and are active in many military
veteran’s service organizations. I am a past All American VFW Post, District, and
State Commander and a proud recipient of the coveted All American VFW Triple
Crown. I have served on numerous committees at the State and National level and
currently appointed as VFW Department of Arkansas Chief of Staff while dutifully
serving a four year elected term on the VFW National Council of Administration
(Board of Directors) and appointed to the National Committee for Finance and
Internal Organization.

I thought it would be appropriate to discuss the relationship between our firm and the City of
Cabot in connection with the potential Franchise Fee and Sales and Use Tax bond issues.
Stephens will assist the City by providing financial information and expertise, will attend
meetings in order to discuss and explain available financing alternatives, so in the end, the
Council will be able to select a financing vehicle that best accomplishes the required goals.
As part of our work, we would ask that the City provide standard information necessary to draft a
Preliminary and Final Official Statement, which will be used in the placement of bonds. In the
event that bonds are eventually sold, the City agrees to designate Stephens as underwriter for
these financings. It is understood that the City will not be obligated to our firm for any cost or
expense in the event bonds are not issued. As in the past, our compensation will be limited
solely to the bonds’ sale, the terms of which are subject to the City’s approval. We agree to pay
all travel, phone and computer expenses relating to our work on these projects. All other costs
associated with the bond’s issuance will be paid from bond proceeds, or from existing funds.

WHEREAS, the Police Department for the City of Cabot, has accumulated a large amount
of outdated records and materials; and

WHEREAS, due to the lack of storage space, it has become necessary to destroy these
documents to allow current data adequate space to be stored; and

WHEREAS, Arkansas Code Annotated §14-59-114 allows for the destruction of said
records if supported by an affidavit signed by the municipal employee performing the destruction
and one (1) council member.

ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: Pursuant to Arkansas Code Annotated §14-59-114, the supporting affidavit
signed by Jackie Davis Chief of Police and James Reid, City Council Member, the City Council
does hereby authorize the destruction of various documents as set forth in the affidavit attached
hereto as Exhibit “A” and incorporated herein by this reference.

SECTION 2: This resolution shall be in full force and effect from and after the date of its
passage.

AFFIDAVIT

A request is hereby made to the City Council for permission to destroy (recycle via compactor
and/or shredder) outdated records and materials of the Cabot Police Department. Due to lack of
storage space, it has become necessary to destroy these documents and allow current data
adequate space to be stored.

Per statute Arkansas Code Annotated § 14-2-204, case files and support documents are to be
maintained for a period of at least seven (7) years; therefore, the Chief of Police requests that
the following support documents dated prior to January 1, 2014 be destroyed:

Arrest Records
Incident Reports
Accident Reports
Jail Logs

Radio Logs

permanently maintained and will comply with Arkansas Code Annotated §§ 12-12-104 and 14-2-
203(b)(1) and that the records related to crimes of violence as defined by Arkansas Code
Annotated § 5-42-203 will be kept permanently. All documents previously mentioned for
destruction are included in the auditing process. Since the City of Cabot is audited annually, the
documentation has already been part of prior audits.

PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
CIVIL ENGINEERING, AND OTHER RELATED PROFESSIONAL SERVICES

THIS AGREEMENT is between the City of Cabot, an Arkansas municipal corporation (City), and Halff
Associates, Inc., a Texas corporation, which is registered to practice Civil Engineering in the State of
Arkansas (Consultant).

RECITALS

A. Pursuant to ACA 19-11-801 et seq., the City of Cabot (City) solicited proposals for a City Engineering
Consultant.

B. After reviewing all proposals, the City has selected Halff Associates, Inc. (Consultant) as the most
qualified Consultant to provide the proposed services in the best interest of the City.

C. Consultant is willing and qualified to perform such services.

TERMS OF AGREEMENT

1. Consultant’s Scope of Services
Consultant shall perform professional consulting services related to Civil and Environmental engineering
and other related engineering needs applicable to the Scope of Services as outlined in “Exhibit A”.

2. Effective Date and Duration

This agreement is effective on execution by both parties and shall expire, unless otherwise terminated or
extended, on December 31, 2020. The City reserves the right to extend this Agreement, upon written mutual
terms, and subject to City Council approval.

3. Consultant’s Tasks, Fees, and Schedules
A. Fee

Fees for services under this Agreement shall be based on time and materials and be pursuant to
the rates shown in Exhibit B. Consultant may increase the rates shown in Exhibit B on an annual
basis, subject to the written approval of the City. Consultant will alert the City when Consultant is
increasing fees. Consultant will bill for progress payments on a monthly basis. In order to
determine the maximum monetary limit for each task, the Consultant will submit a schedule and
a labor hour estimate based on the rates shown in Exhibit B. Consultant will invoice monthly
progress payments based on actual time worked on the project. The maximum monetary limit will
not be exceeded without prior written approval by the City. Projects partially completed may be
paid for in proportion to the degree of completion.

Consultant will be reimbursed for direct charges such as the cost of printing, postage, delivery
services, and sub consultant fees. Direct charges will be billed at cost without any markup. Office
expenses such as computer cost, telephone calls, and overhead expenses are incidental and are
included in the hourly rate shown in Exhibit B.

B. Payment Schedule for Basic Fee
Payments shall be made within thirty (30) days of receipt of monthly billings based on the work

completed. Payment by the City shall release the City from any further obligation for payment to
the Consultant for the service or services performed or expenses incurred as of the date of the
statement of services. Payment shall be made only for work actually completed as of the date of
invoice. Payment shall not be considered acceptance or approval of any work or waiver of any
defects therein.

Cabot City Council Work Session
Veterans Park Event Center
February 1, 2021
6:30 p.m.

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on social distancing
by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot moved the monthly Work Session
to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508 N. Lincoln, as advertised. This allowed for spacing
between chairs, as suggested. The event was successfully streamed through YouTube.
You may view this meeting at https://youtu.be/2TIEA76vmrE.

Council members present were: Ed Long, Michael Jones, Brandon Hillenburg, Maggie
Cope, James Reid, Matt Webber and Ron Waymack. Stephen Redd attended the meeting
via Zoom. Others present: City Attorney Ben Hooper, City Paralegal Jessica Looper and
City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

Mayor Kincade opened the meeting at 6:30 p.m.

Municipal Services Committee Business: (Members are: Long, Reid, Redd & Cope)
As Chairman, Ed Long began his portion of the meeting by introducing those in
attendance who are chairmen of other city commissions. Gary Walker and Tim Joyner
attended from WaterWorks; Greg Sled from the Recreation Commission; and Chad
Young, Chairman of the Planning Commission, attended via Zoom. No one was in
attendance to represent the Advertising & Promotion Commission.
The appointment of Ashley Little to the Recreation Commission was tabled until the
meeting on the 22nd at the request of Ed Long due to Mr. Little being unavailable to
attend tonight’s meeting.
The authorization to enter into an agreement with Stephens, Inc. regarding a potential
bond offering was addressed by Mayor Kincade and Mr. Jack Truemper with Stephens.
Beginning with a town hall meeting on February 22", the City determines to hold multiple
town hall meetings as a means to include the community in planning numerous capital
improvement projects throughout the City. Mr. Truemper explained the City’s 2013 and
2016 bond issues can be restructured to generate an additional 56.5 million in revenue
for new capital projects. These bonds are projected to be paid in full in 2039 replacing
the current bonds projected to be paid in full in 2025, which is a 13 - 14 year extension
assuming no sales tax growth. City sales tax collection has grown over the last several
years from 3.9 million in 2013 to 5.6 million in 2020. This strong increase in collections
has paid down the bonds and produced more equity allowing for this new revenue without
raising taxes. Mr. Truemper went on to explain interest rates are very attractively at low
levels due to the COVID-19 environment. Mayor Kincade reiterated his desire to hear the
public’s ideas and to decide together what the citizens need and want. So far, broadband
for the entire city, purchasing fiber to be leased out, road improvements, animal shelter
improvements, Police Department improvements, and a multi-use building for Parks and
Rec are on the list to be talked about among other items. He explained there is no limit

--- page 2 (OCR) ---
to the number of projects that can be listed on the ballot and each one must be voted on
independently. Only those approved by the voters will move forward. Mr. Truemper
reviewed a timeline of the events necessary for the completion of this bond refunding. A
copy is attached to these minutes. Tentatively, a local election which allows the citizens
of Cabot to decide what projects to fund is scheduled for June 8, 2021. However, all
dates are preliminary and can be changed to accommodate the needs of the City. Should
this bond issue follow the planned timeline, funds will be available in mid-September to
begin each project approved. Motion by James to place this item on the next City Council
Meeting’s agenda, second by Maggie. All members of this committee voted yes. Motion
passed 4-0.

Joe Gunderman asked the committee to renew Halff as the City’s engineering firm for the
New Year. Motion by James to place on the next City Council Meeting’s agenda, second
by Stephen. All members of this committee voted yes. Motion passed 4-0.

Laura Nobles, Public Works Director, explained the Proposed UDC amendments
addressing the indoor and outdoor recreation type uses. Chad Young, Chairman of the
Planning Commission, stated the Planning Commission fully supports these amendments.
Motion by Maggie to place this item on the next City Council Meeting’s agenda, second
by James. All members of this committee voted yes. Motion passed 4-0. Per Laura’s
request, the legislation will move to the meeting on the 225,

Mike Wheeler and Mayor Kincade asked the committee to consider purchasing the
building at 2102 S. 24, This is the building we currently rent and run 25 new animal
services programs out of. The purchase price is $235,000 and $115,000 is necessary for
improvements. Discussion. Motion by James to place this item on the next City Council
Meeting‘s agenda, second by Maggie. All members of this committee voted yes. Motion
passed 4-0.

Budget & Personnel Committee Business: (Members are: Webber, Hillenburg, &
Jones) As Chairman, Matt started his portion of the meeting at 7:06 calling on Calvin
Aldridge with Ellis, Tucker & Aldridge, LLC to review the 2019 City audit. There were no
questions for Mr. Aldridge and no action required by the council.

Police & Fire Committee Business: (Members are: Reid, Hillenburg, Redd & Cope) As
Chairman, James started his portion of the meeting at 7:19. Captain Scott Steely was
asked to address the committee regarding the approval to destroy outdated documents
in compliance with Ark. Code § 14-2-204. Motion by Maggie to place this item on the next
City Council Meeting’s agenda, second by Brandon. All members of this committee voted
yes. Motion passed 4-0.

Community Development Committee Business: (Members are: Long & Reid). No
action.

Military Affairs Committee Business: (Members are: Waymack, Jones & Webber)
Nothing on agenda. No action.

Council Member Brandon Hillenburg asked how it came about that the city increased the
building permit fees by ten cents. Discussion.

The meeting ended at 7:31 p.m. with a motion to adjourn by Stephen, second by James
and a unanimous vote.

Citizen Participation Plan
City of Cabot, Arkansas

A. Participation by Citizens

All citizens, including low- and moderate-income citizens, shall be requested and encouraged

to participate in the assessment of community issues, problems and needs; the identification

of potential solutions; and priority to such issues, problems and needs, as follows:

1. All citizens shall be periodically requested to complete a community needs survey to
identify community and neighborhood issues, problems and needs.

2. All citizens shall be notified by publication and posting of all meetings to discuss the
identified needs, potential solutions and solution priorities.

3. All citizens, particularly low and moderate-income citizens, shall be afforded the
opportunity to serve on various community improvement task forces established by the
City of Cabot.

B. Access to Meetings, Information and Records
Notice of public meetings conducted by the City of Cabot shall be published or posted within
a reasonable number of days prior to such meetings.

Agendas of all such meetings shall be available at the Cabot City Hall for public inspection.

All meetings where CDBG projects or applications are to be discussed shall be published or
posted no less than seven days prior to such meetings and all information and records
concerning such CDBG projects or applications shall be available for public inspection at the
grant administrators office at Central Arkansas Planning and Development District, 902 N.
Center Street, Lonoke, AR 70286.

All meetings will be held at a time and location convenient to potential or actual beneficiaries
which will be accessible to all citizens. The building and site will also be accessible to persons
with disabilities.

C. Specific CDBG Project Information

All citizens shall be provided with information regarding specific CDBG projects through public

meetings and publication of notices which provide all pertinent information regarding any

CDBG project including, but not limited to:

1. The amount of CDBG funds expected to be made available to the City of Cabot for the
current fiscal year, including CDBG funds and anticipated program income;

2. The specific range of activities that may be undertaken with CDBG funds;

3. The estimated amount of CDBG funds to be used for activities that will meet the national
objective of benefit to low-and moderate-income persons, and;

The City of Cabot shall enact a minimum of two (2) public meetings or hearings to be

conducted prior to the submission of any such application and a second public hearing shall
be held near the completion of any CDBG funded activity to obtain citizen input, comments or
opinions with regard to such application(s) and to program or project performance.

The Mayor shall act as the contact person for all questions, comments or concerns expressed
by any citizen with regard to any CDBG program or project and shall forward any such
questions, comments or concerns to the City of Cabot at the next regular meeting of the City
of Cabot immediately following expression of such questions, comments or concerns. The
Mayor or his authorized representative shall also be responsible for transmitting the City of
Cabot response to any such question, comment or concerns to the citizen or citizens
expressing the same.

F. Needs of Non-English Speaking Citizens

The City of Cabot shall conduct the public hearings in a manner to meet the needs of non-
English speaking residents where significant number of non-English speaking residents can
reasonably be expected to participate, the Mayor shall arrange for oral or written translation
of information regarding any CDBG program, application or project upon request by such non-
English speaking persons or representatives of such persons.

G. Compliance/Grievance Procedures

The Mayor shall post a notice at the Cabot City Hall that provides name, telephone number,
address and office hours of the City of Cabot for citizens who wish to file a complaint or
grievance regarding any CDBG program, project or application.

Individuals wishing to submit a complaint or file a grievance concerning activities, of or
application for, CDBG funds may submit a written complaint or grievance to the Mayor.

Center. Council Member Stephen Redd led the prayer and Council Member
Ron Waymack led the Pledge of Allegiance.

Michael Jones, Ron Waymack and Stephen Redd. Also in attendance were

Treasurer Tammy Yocom and IT Director Roger Self.

Prevention to Laura Abbott, Victims’ Right Advocate.

AGREEMENT; TO DECLARE AN EMERGENCY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, the City, in conjunction with Cabot City Beautiful, wishes to conduct
a Household Hazardous Waste Round-up event scheduled for March 2021; and

WHEREAS, quotes from three separate vendors were solicited. CTS Services, Inc
(CTS) provided the lowest firm quote (another provider returned a ranged quote, partly
lower and partly higher). Given the nature of the services at issue and the unknown factor
of how much hazardous waste will be disposed of, it is impossible to say what the final cost
will be and if the amount will be one that requires competitive bidding to be used.

WHEREAS Ark. Code Ann § 14-58-303 et al., provides that the governing body may
waive the requirement of competitive bidding in situations where the procedure is deemed not
feasible or practical.

WHEREAS a service offering the removal and disposal of household hazardous waste
will be directly beneficial to the health, safety, and welfare of the people of Cabot.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: The Mayor and City Clerk~Treasurer are hereby authorized to enter into
an Agreement with CTS Services, Inc. to collect, bulk, containerize, transfer and recycle/dispose
of household hazardous waste during the Household Hazardous Waste Round-up event. The
agreement is authorized to be consistent with the terms in the attached Exhibit A. The City
Council recognizes that the amount of payment to CTS for these services will depend on how
much and what type of hazardous waste is disposed of at the event. Payment to CTS is
authorized to be consistent with the unit costs listed in Exhibit A.

SECTION 2: Competitive bidding for this matter is hereby deemed to be neither
feasible nor practical given both the time constraints and the nature of the project that makes
fixed pricing, and therefore bidding, extremely difficult. In addition, the scope of the project, the

very large variety of types and forms of hazardous waste that could be collected, and the

44

--- page 49 (OCR) ---
unknown factor of how much/what manner of hazardous waste will ultimately be collected
would make going through the competitive bidding process extremely difficult and neither
feasible nor practical.

SECTION 3: The project authorized herein — the timely removal of hazardous waste
from people’s homes - is of direct benefit to the health, safety, and welfare to the residents of
Cabot. A delay in the enactment of this ordinance would necessitate a delay in the clean-up
event, thereby leaving hazardous waste in residents’ homes for a longer period of time.
Therefore, due to the clear risks to the health, safety, and welfare of the residents of Cabot that
would be caused by delaying the enactment of this ordinance, an emergency is hereby declared to

exist and this ordinance shall be in full force and effect from and after its passage.

Municipal Services Committee Business: (Members are: Long, Reid, Redd & Cope)

As Chairman, Ed Long opened this committee meeting asking City Attorney Ben
Hooper to address the Planning Commission's appeal process. Ben explained a developer
has requested to go through the appeals process outlined in the UDC which allows for a
developer to appeal a Planning Commission denial to the City Council. He further
explained, the vote tonight will be to initiate a hearing where the council members will
have a similar role as a judge in this instance. The Council will hear a report from the
Public Works Director, the applicant and any relevant witnesses he wishes to present,
and whomever the Council wants to hear from on the matter. This appeal must be
resolved in one of three ways. They are:

1. Affirm the ruling — (denied)

2. Overrule the denial

3. Grant with conditions
Should new information become available the night of the hearing, this issue must go
back to the Planning Commission. All members of the committee agreed to have this
hearing during the regularly scheduled Council Meeting on April 19, 2021.

attached to these minutes. Cabot WaterWorks Chairman Gary Walker presented their first
quarter report. A copy is attached to these minutes. A person watching by Youtube
submitted a question to Mr. Walker regarding the ending of well water usage (2026).
Discussion. Mr. Hillenburg wanted an explanation regarding the opinion of Waterworks
having a negative atmosphere surrounding builders/developers in general and, more
specifically, those requesting grinder pumps in their developments. Discussion.

RESOLUTION NO. 18 OF 2021

A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING A WAIVER OF THE SERVICE WEAPON AWARD
POLICY; AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

WHEREAS, Arkansas law gives the Mayor the authority to award a retiring law
enforcement officer his or her service pistol. The law also authorizes a retiring law enforcement
officer to purchase his or her duty shotgun at fair market value; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council has promulgated a policy listing various criteria to
guide the Mayor in the award of the service pistol to a retiring law enforcement officer; and

WHEREAS, Officer Don Sims has served the City honorably as a law enforcement
officer for approximately 18 years and is approaching retirement. The policy regarding the
award of a service pistol to a retiring law enforcement officer requires that the officer had served

for 15 consecutive years. Officer Sims has served for approximately 18 years but not
consecutively. He has met all other criteria to qualify for the award of his service pistol; and

WHEREAS, both the Mayor and the City Council wish to recognize Officer Sim’s long
law enforcement career and his many contributions to the safety and welfare of Cabot and its
residents.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF CABOT,
ARKANSAS, THAT:

SECTION 1: The City Council’s promulgated policy is hereby waived for this matter
and this matter only. The Mayor is hereby authorized to award Officer Don Sims his service
pistol upon Officer Sim’s retirement.

SECTION 2: As provided under state law, Officer Sims is also eligible to purchase his
duty shotgun at fair market value upon his retirement.

SECTION 3: This resolution shall be in full force and effect from and after its passage.

Final Plat - Lakewood Subdivision Phase II-A, Lot 71-99 Report:
On 8/26/2020, Lemons Engineering submitted a Final plat for Lakewood Subdivision
Phase II-A, Lots 71-99 for the September 22, 2020 Planning Commission Meeting. The Final plat
was then sent through planning staff tech review for staff comments. Staff comments were received
and on 9/8/2020, a staff letter was sent to Lemons Engineering with staff comments from the tech
review. On 9/16/2020, Lemons Engineering submitted a revised copy of the Final plat and a letter
addressing the tech review comment letter dated 9/8/2020. On 9/18/2020, the Public Works office
emailed the Planning Commission packet out to the planning commission members and city. On
the same day Lemons Engineering submitted to the Public Works office another revised Final plat.
Lemons Engineering had made a few more revisions to the Final plat. On 9/21/2020, Mr. Jim
Green emailed some field density tests for the proposed lots and parts of the streets.
On 9/22/2020, the Planning Commission held their regular scheduled meeting. The Final
Plat for Lakewood Subdivision Phase II-A, Lots 71-99 was on the meeting’s agenda. The Final
plat was brought up for discussion. Staff gave the staff report, the commission chairman asked if
there was anyone in attendance for or against the item. No representative was in attendance. A
motion was made by Ms. Bird to table the Final plat until the next month due to there being too
many outstanding items that had not been fully addressed with a second by Mr. Loe, the motion
passed with a 5-0 vote. Later that evening about 9:12 p.m., I received an email from Mr. Green
apologizing for not being at the planning commission meeting. He stated he had his dates mixed
up on when the meeting was scheduled. Mr. Green also stated that he did not have the street
complete in order for the city to accept the subdivision.
On 9/23/2020, a staff letter was sent to Lemons Engineering regarding the Planning
Commission’s decision to table the Final plat and listed the outstanding items that still needed to
be addressed by the developer. On 9/30/2020, Lemons Engineering submitted another revised
Final plat for Lakewood Subdivision Phase II-A for the October 27, 2020 Planning Commission
Meeting agenda. The Final plat was sent through planning staff tech review for staff comment
again. On 10/9/2020, a staff letter was sent to Lemons Engineering regarding outstanding items
that still needed to be addressed. Lemons Engineering submitted a revised Final plat and letter on
10/19/2020, stating the outstanding items from the staff letter dated 10/9/2020 were addressed. On
10/23/2020, the Public Works office emailed the planning commission packet out to the planning
commission members and city. On 10/26/2020, Lemons Engineering submitted another copy of
the Final plat stating there were additional items that were revised on the plat.
On 10/27/2020, the Planning Commission held their regular scheduled meeting. The Final
Plat for Lakewood Subdivision Phase II-A, Lots 71-99 was on the meeting’s agenda. The Final
plat was brought up for discussion. The commission members discussed the need for a 2nd access
to the subdivision with Mr. Green, per fire department code. Commission members asked Mr.
Green if he had reached out to Mr. Feland, the owner of the property next to the bowling alley and
fitness center, in order to acquire property for a 2nd ingress/egress access. Mr. Green stated, no, he
had not. After a lengthy discussion about a 2nd access, the commission asked Mr. Green to acquire
additional property for a 2nd access to Hwy 321 and to provide a drawing of the 2nd access prior to
bringing the Final plat back for any action. A motion to table the final plat due to too many

outstanding items and a 2nd access to Hwy 321 was made by Mr. Loe with a second by Mr. Moudy,
the motion passed with a 5-0 vote. Mr. Young, the planning commission chairman, advised Mr.
Green to get with staff with a planned and designed 2nd access to Hwy 321 for the subdivision. On
10/28/2020, a staff letter was sent to Lemons Engineering regarding Planning Commission’s
decision to table the Final plat and listed the outstanding items.
Over the next couple of months, Mr. Green sent several emails with information that he
asked me to give to the planning commission members to review for when he is placed back on
the planning commission’s agenda. Mr. Green was placed on the regularly scheduled February
planning commission agenda. Mr. Green had stated that he had acquired additional property for a
2nd ingress/egress for the subdivision. On 2/19/2021, the Public Works office emailed the planning
commission packet out to the planning commission members and city.
On 2/23/2021, the Planning Commission held their regularly scheduled meeting. The Final
plat for Lakewood Subdivision Phase II-A, Lots 71-99 was on the meeting’s agenda. The Final
plat was brought up for discussion. The commission and Mr. Green again discussed a 2nd
ingress/egress. Mr. Green stated that he had reached out to the property owner to the East of the

Green stated, yes, that he needed a vote tonight. Commissioner Prater made a motion to approve
the Final plat. Commissioner Loe made a second, the motion failed with a 0-5 vote.

Commission a motion to approve the final plat was denied with a 0-5 vote. The letter also stated
that the commission felt that the development was not ready for final plat approval and that several
items were still outstanding. The letter listed the outstanding items. On 3/4/2021, I received an
email from Mr. Green requesting an appeal of the Planning Commission’s decision regarding Final

City Attorney’s office. After speaking with Ben Hooper, I emailed Mr. Green on 3/8/2021, to
explain the process to appeal the decision of the Planning Commission. I also called and spoke to
Mr. Green to explain the process for his appeal.

Phase I and 3 accesses
The access issue started in 2005. Planning Comm demanded I remove 2 of the 3 entrances I had recently installed along
my property adjoining 321. Prior to annexation I had applied and received permits from ARDOT. I spent several
thousand in drainage const on those entrances. I complied and removed all but 1.
I began the process of developing the residential area. I submitted a sketch plat showing 200+ lots utilizing the single
entrance. At same time, submitted a preml plat of Ph I showing 56 lots utilizing the fore mentioned single entrance. I now
realize even Ph I was not in compliance with fire code 30 lot restriction.
If I had been confronted with the 2 access need back in 2005, I could have easily used 1 of the lots in Ph I to provide a
secondary access thru one of the 3 321 outlets thru the commercial area. I would have lost a $25,000 lot vs the $35,000
lot lost in Ph II.

Phase II
I submitted prelm plat for Ph II. During Plan Comm discussion, the fire dept intervened by addressing the need for more
than 1 access. Mr. Lemons and Chief Smart had discussions on the matter. Chief Smart agreed that a planned street to
my property line satisfied the state fire code for second access in future development. Lemons added the street to the
preliminary plat and redrew the overall sketch plat per the commission’s request. ( I have Chief Smarts sworn statement)
The added street R/W cost me a $35,000 lot but decided not to object. Although, I felt it was unfair considering the
planning comm in 2005 was provided a sketch plat showing 200 homes with the same single access. I was convinced the
second access issue was over. The planning commission now had a sketch plat showing 200 lots with the same 321
accesss as well as the agreed on R/W adjoining lot 70. All was well ????
I began const of Ph II which involved 14 lots on N side of lake and 27 lots on S side. In the fall of 2017, weather was very
close to shutting us down. I decided to go forward with recording the N side 14 lots. Rains had shut down all dirt moving
operations.

Phase II and IIA
I continued to do dirt work on the occasional dry spells between rains. During the dirt moving portion of the work on both
sides of lake we dug, hauled, and compacted over 290,000 cu yds of material ( equivalent to 21,714 large dump truck
loads ). In Mar 2018, I contacted Mr. Clem that I was hoping it would shortly be dry enough to get started with utilities on
S side. Had several email discussions with Clem and Gunderman. I knew there would need to be inspections of utility
work. Rains continued to haunt us continually thru 2020.

Phase IIA Final
Now comes to requesting final plat approval. We constructed all of Ph II ( both sides of lake ) per the preliminary plat
previously approved. Planning commission questioned Chief Smarts 2015 approval the prelim plat. They felt it needed
revising. Prelm plat approval of the area was not enough.
The city advised me in the PC comment letter of 10-28-20 as to what they expected me to provide. Again, I felt they had
no right to abandon their approval of prem plat of PH II. But I have 11 lots sold and many are pre-sold with families trying
to make plans as where they hope to be in the NEAR future.

To committed lot buyers of Ph IIA, Lakewood Subd. -- I ask for your understanding.
I realize some of you have lot contracts with me dating back to the fall of 2019. This story will hopefully explain why you have had such
a long wait.
Lakewood work started originally in 2004 along my 321 frontage. There was an existing single access to 321 located at my NW corner.
I applied and received ARDOT permits for 2 additional access points onto 321. During the development along frontage, the city forced
me to tear out and abandon 2 of the 3 access points. I went to planning comm, board of adjustment as well as mayors office attempting
to keep the 3 access points. Did not succeed even though I had spent several thousand on drainage under those drives.
I later submitted a sketch plat for the residential area that clearly showed 200+ lots using this same single access point they allowed me
earlier. Also received approval of prelm plat containing 56 lots for Ph I.
Time for PH II with lots on both sides of Lake. This is first mention of requiring a plan for a second access point. Mr Lemons visited Fire
dept concerning second access. Cabot Fire Dept and Mr. Lemons decided that a planned R/W to my N bdry would satisfy the required
“planned” fire access. The commission asked Mr. Lemons to prepare a new entire subdivision sketch plat showing the new planned
access. Which was provided to planning comm. Planning commission accepted the plan and approved the prelim plat. All concerned
incld planning comm assumed the fire code access question was no longer an issue. I accepted this solution although it cost me the
loss of an 85’ lot. I assumed the approval of the 2005 sketch plat showing 200 lots with a single access as well as the 2015 sketch plat
which showed 200 plus lots with single access as well as the planned access added per fire dept. should have finally addressed this
issue. Fire code has been same since long before I started Lakewood.
I began planning Ph II in 2015. Due to the tremendous amount of dirt work during record setting rainfalls we were really behind.
Example: Dirt work on Phase I took 13 months and that was a dry year ( and that was before we could start normal subdivision work. I
decided to concentrate on the N 14 lots and complete the S 29 lots when the weather allowed. Final plat on the N. side of lake was
approved 9-8-17.
I continued to do dirt work on the S 28 lots thru out the winter months but only able to work between rains. I was able to keep it draining
and finished some of the off street dirt work . I have a backhoe, track hoe, dozer, and dump truck but I’m the only operator so during
those scarce few dryer days I was not able to get much done. Still too wet to allow larger contractors to move in and justify only a day or
2 between rains.
In March 2018, it was still wet but hoped weather would allow start of utility work soon. I continued with dirt work but knew city would
need to inspect installation of utilities so I contacted Mr. Clem to inform him we hope to get started soon on finishing S side work
needing city inspections. The city din’t require any more documentation until ready for final plat. We still had some dirt work to
complete but it would not interrupt utility work.
Again due to unusually wet spring and summer 2020, our street and utility work went slow. I lacked only approx. 4 weeks work in the fall
of 2019 when weather caught us again. The street and utility work was finished this week. Took us 15 months to finish work I had told
builders and lot buyers 4 to 6 weeks. I had projected early in 2020. They have been extremely patient and understanding but can’t and
shouldn’t much longer even though they realize I’ve gone as fast as weather would permit.
If it rains in fall , winter, or spring today, we might be able to work after 4 days of dry time. But another rain in 3 days kills that!!! Another
rain on top of the previous rain needs 6 days. And so forth???
If the current planninjg comm believes the previous 2 planning comm were in error, they need to address the situation in that light. Per
the info I provided, there are currently many developed areas more out of compliance than mine.
The sketch plats are provided to the planning comm to review the basics of the overall plan. The access issue should have been
addressed in 2005 but at that point the planning comm had recently forced me to tear out 2 of the 3 accesses on my property adjoining
321. I could have easily provided another street to 321. I may have had to sacrifice a residential lot but I did same in 2015.

On 8/26/2020, Lemons Engineering submitted a Final plat for Lakewood Subdivision
Phase II-A, Lots 71-99 for the September 22, 2020 Planning Commission Meeting. The Final plat

review. On 9/16/2020, Lemons Engineering submitted a revised copy of the Final plat and a letter
addressing the tech review comment letter dated 9/8/2020. On 9/18/2020, the Public Works office
emailed the Planning Commission packet out to the planning commission members and city. On
the same day Lemons Engineering submitted to the Public Works office another revised Final plat.
Lemons Engineering had made a few more revisions to the Final plat. On 9/21/2020, Mr. Jim
Green emailed some field density tests for the proposed lots and parts of the streets.
On 9/22/2020, the Planning Commission held their regular scheduled meeting. The Final
Plat for Lakewood Subdivision Phase II-A, Lots 71-99 was on the meeting’s agenda. The Final
plat was brought up for discussion. Staff gave the staff report, the commission chairman asked if
there was anyone in attendance for or against the item. No representative was in attendance. A
motion was made by Ms. Bird to table the Final plat until the next month due to there being too
many outstanding items that had not been fully addressed with a second by Mr. Loe, the motion
passed with a 5-0 vote. Later that evening about 9:12 p.m., I received an email from Mr. Green
apologizing for not being at the planning commission meeting. He stated he had his dates mixed
up on when the meeting was scheduled. Mr. Green also stated that he did not have the street
complete in order for the city to accept the subdivision.
On 9/23/2020, a staff letter was sent to Lemons Engineering regarding the Planning
Commission’s decision to table the Final plat and listed the outstanding items that still needed to
be addressed by the developer. On 9/30/2020, Lemons Engineering submitted another revised
Final plat for Lakewood Subdivision Phase II-A for the October 27, 2020 Planning Commission
Meeting agenda. The Final plat was sent through planning staff tech review for staff comment
again. On 10/9/2020, a staff letter was sent to Lemons Engineering regarding outstanding items
that still needed to be addressed. Lemons Engineering submitted a revised Final plat and letter on
10/19/2020, stating the outstanding items from the staff letter dated 10/9/2020 were addressed. On
10/23/2020, the Public Works office emailed the planning commission packet out to the planning
commission members and city. On 10/26/2020, Lemons Engineering submitted another copy of
the Final plat stating there were additional items that were revised on the plat.
On 10/27/2020, the Planning Commission held their regular scheduled meeting. The Final
Plat for Lakewood Subdivision Phase II-A, Lots 71-99 was on the meeting’s agenda. The Final
plat was brought up for discussion. The commission members discussed the need for a 2nd access
to the subdivision with Mr. Green, per fire department code. Commission members asked Mr.
Green if he had reached out to Mr. Feland, the owner of the property next to the bowling alley and
fitness center, in order to acquire property for a 2nd ingress/egress access. Mr. Green stated, no, he
had not. After a lengthy discussion about a 2nd access, the commission asked Mr. Green to acquire
additional property for a 2nd access to Hwy 321 and to provide a drawing of the 2nd access prior to
bringing the Final plat back for any action. A motion to table the final plat due to too many

again. On 10/9/2020, a staff letter was sent to Lemons Engineering regarding outstanding items

10/19/2020, stating the outstanding items from the staff letter dated 10/9/2020 were addressed. On

commission members and city. On 10/26/2020, Lemons Engineering submitted another copy of
the Final plat stating there were additional items that were revised on the plat.

plat was brought up for discussion. The commission members discussed the need for a 2"4 access

Scope of Services/Work
Since Federal funds will be used for the Project, an environmental review and appropriate
documentation is required in accordance with the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), 23
Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 771, and ARDOT requirements. This scope of work and
fee estimate are based on the assumption that the proposed improvements would meet the
requirements of 23 CFR 771.117, Categorical Exclusions. The Project is assumed to be
considered a “c-list” CE project based on 23 CFR 771.117(c)(3) construction of bicycle and pedestrian
lanes, paths, and facilities. In the event it is determined by ARDOT or the Federal Highway
Administration (FHWA) that a CE is not the appropriate level of documentation for the Project,
Consultant will notify the Owner and a supplemental scope of work will be prepared to allow completion
of other suitable documentation.
The following tasks will be necessary to receive a CE determination from ARDOT:
A. Project Scoping
Consultant will perform project scoping in coordination with ARDOT and the City of Cabot to initiate
the CE determination process. This task includes one meeting with the Owner and/or ARDOT, if
necessary.
B. Data Collection and Environmental Constraints Mapping
Consultant will obtain digital environmental information available from appropriate local, state,
and federal agencies. Data collected through this task will be stored in Geographical Information
Systems (GIS) format. Consultant will perform a site visit of the Project area to document
existing conditions. This task includes taking on-site photographs. It is assumed the Project
corridor is accessible and right of entry from private property owners will not be necessary.
C. Natural and Physical Environment
Review protected species lists from the Arkansas Natural Heritage Commission (ANHC) and the
United States Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) for Lonoke County. Conclusions will be
made, based on general observations from a visual survey and the literature review, regarding
whether preferred habitat or designated critical habitat for any listed threatened and endangered
species is present within the Project area, whether any listed species is likely to occur, and
whether there is a potential impact or effect to listed species.
A jurisdictional determination of waters of the United States, including wetlands, will be made
within the anticipated ROW and areas anticipated to be disturbed by construction for the Project.
This determination will include delineation of the boundaries and ordinary high-water mark of
jurisdictional waters within the Project area.
Document floodplains, aquifers, navigable waters, and state or federal scenic rivers within the
Project area.
Determine farmland impacts. Identification of farmland impacts shall be in accordance with the
Farmland Protection Policy Act (FPPA) (7 USC 4201 et. seq.) and guidance on addressing FPPA
requirements, which includes determining whether the project is exempt or completion of form
AD 1006 or CPA 106 as appropriate.
Identify any hazardous waste sites, leaking underground storage tanks, oil/gas wells, or other
potentially contaminated sites in the Project area. This task will include review of environmental
regulatory databases and visual observations of the Project site.

--- page 27 (text layer) ---

D. Cultural Resources
Identify cultural resources in the Project area in compliance with the requirements of Section 106
of the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA) [16 USC § 470(f)] and implementing
regulations (36 CFR Part 800). A records review will be conducted to identify recorded
archeological or historic sites within the area of potential effects (APE) for the Project.
E. Socioeconomics
Document public service facilities and community resources such as parks, medical facilities,
churches and schools adjacent to the Project. Document the population and income characteristics
of the Project area, and identify potential Environmental Justice (EJ) and Limited English
Proficiency (LEP) populations as well as potential impacts on community cohesion.
F. Air Quality
Consultant will document the project area attainment status relative to the National Ambient Air
Quality Standards (NAAQS), as well as project exemption from an air conformity determination,
project exemption from a traffic air quality analysis, and project consistency with the
Transportation Improvement Program/Statewide Transportation Improvement Program
(TIP/STIP).
G. Agency Coordination
Consultant will prepare and submit requests for comments from appropriate resource agencies.
Consultant will include a project description and relevant information regarding potential impacts
to resources subject to regulatory protection. Correspondence will be in the form of a letter with
appropriate attachments distributed via regular mail for review and comment by the following
resource agencies as appropriate: ANHC, USFWS Arkansas Ecological Services Field Office,
U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Natural Resources Conservation Commission (NRCS),
and the State Historic Preservation Office.
H. CE Documentation
Prepare and submit CE documentation addressing resources and issues as described above for
ARDOT review and approval.

Deliverables will be in accordance with ARDOT standards and guidelines for CE projects and
will include the following:

• Draft and final CE Documentation

hard copies will be provided upon request by the Owner and/or ARDOT.
